To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a method for simultaneous quantification of muramic acid (MA), mannosamine (MAA), glucosamine (GlcN) and galactosamime (GalN) was optimised by reducing the retention time and optimising the separation of MA and MAA by modifying the mobilephase.
the retention time was reduced and the separation of the amino sugars was optimized by modifying the mobile-phase composition.
a reverse-phase HPLC method was improved for simultaneous determination of amino sugars by OPA derivatization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimisation and validation of a method for the simultaneous quantification of amino sugars in soil and plant samples.
the optimisation of a method for simultaneous determination of four amino sugars, which is a prerequisite for the application of this method in the field of environmental analysis.
the development of a sensitive, specific and reliable method for the quantification of amino sugars in soil and plant samples.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the optimised method provides a fast and reliable separation of amino sugars, and it is applicable for the quantification of muramic acid in soil and plant samples.
the proposed HPLC method is a reliable and sensitive method for quantifying amino sugars.

the method presented here can be applied to a wide range of soils and plants, and it is suitable for quantifying amino sugars in the range of approximately 1 to 100 mg amino sugars per gram dry weight.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the method described in this study can be used to determine the amino sugars in soil and plant samples with high precision and sensitivity.
the developed method is simple and reliable for the simultaneous quantification of amino sugars in soil and plant samples.

we developed a new method for the simultaneous determination and quantification of muramic acid (MUR), mannosamine (MAN), glucosamine (GLN) and galactosamime (GAL) in soil and plant samples via HPLC-FLD with OPA pre-column derivatisation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the method is applicable for routine analysis in soil and plant samples.
the method is simple and robust.
the method is applicable for the quantification of muramic acid as well as the other amino sugars in soil and plant samples.
